ideas.description: Control run for H1.4.1, and the epoch-slope point for H1. Start from A1a (E001 tip) and change only the epoch count, from 8.5 to 8.0. Scale the LR and lookahead/EMA schedule to the new total step count the same way the recipe already does. Leave everything else byte-identical. Log the per-seed accuracies.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.80 s (-5.5 to -6%, since 1 epoch is about 0.85 s). Accuracy about 0.751-0.754 (-0.15 to -0.4 pp vs 0.7549). If it is >=0.753 it becomes the new tip. Either way it measures the local accuracy-per-epoch slope that every later epoch-cut idea depends on, and it is the baseline for the brightness/contrast and label-smoothing ideas.

ideas.description: Take the 8.0-epoch recipe from the control idea and add light brightness/contrast jitter in the existing GPU-side augmentation. Per image, multiply by a contrast factor drawn uniformly from [0.85, 1.15] around the per-image mean, then add a brightness offset drawn uniformly from [-0.1, 0.1] (in normalized units), before the flip/translate step. Apply it to training batches only and keep it a single fused elementwise op. Change nothing else.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp over the 8.0-epoch control, giving about 0.753-0.756 (feasible). Time within +0.5% of the control, about 6.80-6.85 s, because the op is cheap. If accuracy does not beat the control by more than about 0.2 pp (the perturbation-noise level), H1.4.1 is refuted.

ideas.description: On the 8.0-epoch recipe, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. This tests whether the reference hyperparameters, which were tuned at 8.5 epochs, leave accuracy on the table at shorter schedules. Shorter training usually wants less regularization.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp over the 8.0-epoch control. Time identical to the control (about 6.80 s). If the gain is >=0.2 pp, also retune at 7.5 epochs. If accuracy falls, ls 0.3 is near-optimal and epoch cuts need another source of accuracy.

ideas.description: Start from A1a. Make the optimizer fused: torch.optim.SGD(fused=True) if PyTorch 2.4 accepts it for this param-group setup, otherwise foreach=True. Wrap the optimizer step plus the lookahead/EMA update in a single torch.compile'd function and warm it up in build on synthetic gradients. Keep the epochs (8.5) and all hyperparameters unchanged. This also tests the E004 power-cap lesson, which predicts little gain from cutting overhead alone.
ideas.expected: Time -0.3 to -1.5% (about 7.11-7.20 s), most likely short of the >=2% that H3.1.1 predicts, which would refute it and confirm the energy-bound model. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp, from floating-point reordering only. If time falls by >=2%, the power-cap model is wrong about optimizer memory traffic, and more fusion is worth pursuing.

ideas.description: Start from A1a (8.5 epochs). From the start of epoch 3, for each batch of 1024: (1) run a no-grad forward through the compiled net in train mode, with BN running-stat updates disabled, and get per-example losses; (2) keep the 614 highest-loss examples (a fixed size, so the shapes stay static); (3) run the normal forward+backward and optimizer step on those 614 only. Compile and warm up the 614-shape train step in build. Keep the LR schedule tied to the step count, which does not change.
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -6%: each step costs about 0.93x a full step after epoch 2, and less GPU energy. Accuracy -0.3 to -1.0 pp, likely infeasible at 8.5 epochs. The value of the run is the exchange rate. If accuracy loss per % of time saved beats the epoch-cut rate (about 0.35 pp per 6%), combine it with +0.5 epochs. Otherwise H2.3 is refuted for this data size.

structured_output.summary:
I added five ideas, which brings the queue to seven. Nothing was dropped: none of the queued hypotheses is settled yet.

**Where things stand.** The current best is still E001 at 7.22 s with accuracy 0.7549. That clears the 0.753 bar by only about 0.19 pp, and E003–E005 showed that small recipe changes alone move the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp.

**What this means for the ideas.** E004 showed the GPU sits at its 400 W power cap, so only cuts to GPU work shorten training. The main lever is therefore fewer epochs: one epoch is about 0.85 s, roughly 12% of the run. Fewer epochs need extra accuracy from somewhere, so most of the new ideas aim there.

**New ideas, in priority order:**
- **Priority 5:** Rerun the current best recipe at 8.0 epochs with no other change. If it stays at or above 0.753 it becomes the new best; either way it measures how much accuracy one epoch buys, and it is the baseline for the next two ideas.
- **Priority 4:** Add light brightness/contrast jitter at 8.0 epochs. This tests H1.4.1 against that baseline.
- **Priority 3:** Lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 at 8.0 epochs. The reference settings were tuned at 8.5 epochs and may leave accuracy on the table at shorter runs.
- **Priority 2 (explore):** Use a fused optimizer and compile the optimizer step together with the EMA update. I expect less than the 2% gain H3.1.1 predicts, which would confirm the power-cap explanation.
- **Priority 2 (explore):** Selective backprop, which tests H2.3.1. From epoch 3, only the 614 highest-loss images in each batch of 1024 get a backward pass; the run measures the accuracy cost per second saved.

**Kept in the queue:**
- I007 (train at 24 → 28 → 32 px over the run) fits the power-cap finding well.
- I008 (batch size 2000) is now lower value. E004 suggests that removing per-step overhead does little on this GPU, so I didn't add more ideas of that kind.

**Not added:** I left out a Muon optimizer test (H5.1.1) because it is unlikely to cut time.
